correctness.rationale: The incoming-ancestor partition at size three is exhaustive; algebra gives an exact factorization with strict sign classification on 0<p,q<1. originality.rationale: No equivalent finite three-person, two-dose expected-case threshold or all-size high-seeding sign law was found in the accessible earlier primary literature and public research records. These statements are neither the classical susceptibility-set formula nor the deterministic large-population allocation theorem; priority remains provisional for unreadable household paper full texts.
residual_risks: Detailed full texts of the 1997, 2002, and 2004 household-allocation papers were not accessible; one might prove a stronger theorem subsuming the claimed boundary.
The result is a sharp small-household specialization of a classical final-size framework, not a claim that generic vaccination-concentration phenomena or susceptibility-set methods are new.
Independent priority and epidemiological interpretation have not been validated.

value.rationale: A precisely motivated finite allocation ambiguity is resolved at its smallest nontrivial household size, including a sharp two-parameter phase boundary and exact counterexamples to transfer of household threshold-optimal heuristics to independent-introduction final-case minimization. The all-size np=2 asymptotic frontier extends its explanatory reach. Biological and historical limitations are stated.
